    Parallel Kalman Filter & SSM Natural Parameters¶

    This notebook demonstrates the parallel (associative-scan) Kalman filter and smoother, the Joseph-form covariance update, and the natural/expectation parameter representations of linear-Gaussian state-space models.

    What you'll learn:

    1. Running gaussx.parallel_kalman_filter and gaussx.parallel_rts_smoother
    2. Verifying equivalence with the sequential Kalman filter
    3. The Joseph-form covariance update for numerical stability
    4. Converting SSM parameters to natural parameters (BlockTriDiag precision)
    5. Converting smoother output to expectation parameters and back

    Background: why parallelism matters¶

    The standard Kalman filter is inherently sequential: each step depends on the previous filtered state. On modern accelerators (GPU/TPU) this sequential bottleneck limits throughput for long time series.

    The associative-scan formulation (Sarkka & Garcia-Fernandez, 2021) reformulates the Kalman recursion as a parallel prefix sum over a semigroup of affine transformations. This enables $O(\log T)$ parallel depth instead of $O(T)$ sequential steps, while producing identical results up to floating-point precision.

    In gaussx, parallel_kalman_filter and parallel_rts_smoother provide the same interface as their sequential counterparts but use dense array operations that are faster on GPU/TPU for long sequences.

    In [1]:
    Copied! 
    from __future__ import annotations

import warnings


warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", message=r".*IProgress.*")

import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

import gaussx


jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True)
    from __future__ import annotations import warnings warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", message=r".*IProgress.*") import jax import jax.numpy as jnp import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import gaussx jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True)

    Define the model¶

    We reuse the damped oscillator from the sequential Kalman filter notebook. The 2D state ($D_x = 2$) $\mathbf{x}_t = [\text{position}, \text{velocity}]^\top$ follows a discretized spring-mass-damper system, and only position is observed with noise ($D_y = 1$), with $\mathbf{x}_t = \mathbf{F} \mathbf{x}_{t-1} + \boldsymbol{\eta}_t$ and $\mathbf{y}_t = \mathbf{H} \mathbf{x}_t + \boldsymbol{\varepsilon}_t$.

    • $\mathbf{F}$: discretized spring-mass-damper transition
    • $\mathbf{H} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$ (observe position only)
    • $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\eta$: model noise driving the oscillator
    • $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\varepsilon = [0.5]$: observation noise variance
    In [2]:
    Copied! 
    # Δt
time_step = 0.1
# T
num_steps = 200

# Damped oscillator: omega=1.0 rad/s, damping gamma=0.15
angular_frequency, damping = 1.0, 0.15
# F = [[1, Δt], [−ω² Δt, 1 − γ Δt]]
transition = jnp.array(
    [
        [1.0, time_step],
        [-(angular_frequency**2) * time_step, 1.0 - damping * time_step],
    ]
)

# Observation matrix (observe position only)
# H ∈ ℝ^{D_y×D_x}
obs_operator = jnp.array([[1.0, 0.0]])

# Model noise covariance
# Σ_η = q_c [[Δt³/3, Δt²/2], [Δt²/2, Δt]]
noise_spectral_density = 0.3
model_noise_covariance = noise_spectral_density * jnp.array(
    [[time_step**3 / 3, time_step**2 / 2], [time_step**2 / 2, time_step]]
)

# Observation noise covariance
# Σ_ε ∈ ℝ^{D_y×D_y}
obs_noise_covariance = jnp.array([[0.5]])

print("F =\n", transition)
print("H =", obs_operator)
print("Σ_η =\n", model_noise_covariance)
print("Σ_ε =", obs_noise_covariance)
    # Δt time_step = 0.1 # T num_steps = 200 # Damped oscillator: omega=1.0 rad/s, damping gamma=0.15 angular_frequency, damping = 1.0, 0.15 # F = [[1, Δt], [−ω² Δt, 1 − γ Δt]] transition = jnp.array( [ [1.0, time_step], [-(angular_frequency**2) * time_step, 1.0 - damping * time_step], ] ) # Observation matrix (observe position only) # H ∈ ℝ^{D_y×D_x} obs_operator = jnp.array([[1.0, 0.0]]) # Model noise covariance # Σ_η = q_c [[Δt³/3, Δt²/2], [Δt²/2, Δt]] noise_spectral_density = 0.3 model_noise_covariance = noise_spectral_density * jnp.array( [[time_step**3 / 3, time_step**2 / 2], [time_step**2 / 2, time_step]] ) # Observation noise covariance # Σ_ε ∈ ℝ^{D_y×D_y} obs_noise_covariance = jnp.array([[0.5]]) print("F =\n", transition) print("H =", obs_operator) print("Σ_η =\n", model_noise_covariance) print("Σ_ε =", obs_noise_covariance)
    F =
 [[ 1.     0.1  ]

H = [[1. 0.]]
Σ_η =

    Simulate data¶

    Generate $T = 200$ time steps from the model. The true trajectory is sampled from the generative process so the Kalman filter assumptions are satisfied.

    In [3]:
    Copied! 
    key = jax.random.PRNGKey(42)


def simulate_step(carry, key_t):
    state = carry
    k1, k2 = jax.random.split(key_t)
    # η_t ~ 𝒩(0, Σ_η)
    model_noise = jax.random.multivariate_normal(
        k1, jnp.zeros(2), model_noise_covariance
    )
    # x_t = F x_{t−1} + η_t
    new_state = transition @ state + model_noise
    # ε_t ~ 𝒩(0, Σ_ε)
    obs_noise = jax.random.multivariate_normal(k2, jnp.zeros(1), obs_noise_covariance)
    # y_t = H x_t + ε_t
    obs_t = obs_operator @ new_state + obs_noise
    return new_state, (new_state, obs_t)


# x_0
true_init_state = jnp.array([3.0, 0.0])  # displaced from equilibrium, at rest
keys = jax.random.split(key, num_steps)
_, (true_states, observations) = jax.lax.scan(simulate_step, true_init_state, keys)

times = jnp.arange(num_steps) * time_step
true_position = true_states[:, 0]

print("true_states shape:", true_states.shape)
print("observations shape:", observations.shape)
    key = jax.random.PRNGKey(42) def simulate_step(carry, key_t): state = carry k1, k2 = jax.random.split(key_t) # η_t ~ 𝒩(0, Σ_η) model_noise = jax.random.multivariate_normal( k1, jnp.zeros(2), model_noise_covariance ) # x_t = F x_{t−1} + η_t new_state = transition @ state + model_noise # ε_t ~ 𝒩(0, Σ_ε) obs_noise = jax.random.multivariate_normal(k2, jnp.zeros(1), obs_noise_covariance) # y_t = H x_t + ε_t obs_t = obs_operator @ new_state + obs_noise return new_state, (new_state, obs_t) # x_0 true_init_state = jnp.array([3.0, 0.0]) # displaced from equilibrium, at rest keys = jax.random.split(key, num_steps) _, (true_states, observations) = jax.lax.scan(simulate_step, true_init_state, keys) times = jnp.arange(num_steps) * time_step true_position = true_states[:, 0] print("true_states shape:", true_states.shape) print("observations shape:", observations.shape)

    Copied! 
    # μ_x,0 = 0
prior_mean = jnp.zeros(2)
# Σ_x,0 = 4 I
prior_covariance = jnp.eye(2) * 4.0

# Parallel filter
par_filter_state = gaussx.parallel_kalman_filter(
    transition,
    obs_operator,
    model_noise_covariance,
    obs_noise_covariance,
    observations,
    prior_mean,
    prior_covariance,
)

print("Parallel filtered means shape:", par_filter_state.filtered_means.shape)
print("Parallel log-likelihood:", par_filter_state.log_likelihood)

    Compare with sequential Kalman filter¶

    The parallel and sequential implementations should produce identical results (up to floating-point precision). We verify this by comparing filtered means, covariances, and the log-likelihood.

    In [6]:
    Copied! 
    # Sequential filter
seq_filter_state = gaussx.kalman_filter(
    transition,
    obs_operator,
    model_noise_covariance,
    obs_noise_covariance,
    observations,
    prior_mean,
    prior_covariance,
)

# Sequential smoother
seq_smooth_means, seq_smooth_covs = gaussx.rts_smoother(seq_filter_state, transition)

# Compare filtered means
mean_diff = jnp.max(
    jnp.abs(par_filter_state.filtered_means - seq_filter_state.filtered_means)
)
print(f"Max abs diff (filtered means): {mean_diff:.2e}")

# Compare filtered covariances
cov_diff = jnp.max(
    jnp.abs(par_filter_state.filtered_covs - seq_filter_state.filtered_covs)
)
print(f"Max abs diff (filtered covs):  {cov_diff:.2e}")

# Compare log-likelihoods
ll_diff = jnp.abs(par_filter_state.log_likelihood - seq_filter_state.log_likelihood)
print(f"Abs diff (log-likelihood):     {ll_diff:.2e}")

# Compare smoothed means
smooth_mean_diff = jnp.max(jnp.abs(par_smooth_means - seq_smooth_means))
print(f"Max abs diff (smoothed means): {smooth_mean_diff:.2e}")

# Compare smoothed covariances
smooth_cov_diff = jnp.max(jnp.abs(par_smooth_covs - seq_smooth_covs))
print(f"Max abs diff (smoothed covs):  {smooth_cov_diff:.2e}")
    # Sequential filter seq_filter_state = gaussx.kalman_filter( transition, obs_operator, model_noise_covariance, obs_noise_covariance, observations, prior_mean, prior_covariance, ) # Sequential smoother seq_smooth_means, seq_smooth_covs = gaussx.rts_smoother(seq_filter_state, transition) # Compare filtered means mean_diff = jnp.max( jnp.abs(par_filter_state.filtered_means - seq_filter_state.filtered_means) ) print(f"Max abs diff (filtered means): {mean_diff:.2e}") # Compare filtered covariances cov_diff = jnp.max( jnp.abs(par_filter_state.filtered_covs - seq_filter_state.filtered_covs) ) print(f"Max abs diff (filtered covs): {cov_diff:.2e}") # Compare log-likelihoods ll_diff = jnp.abs(par_filter_state.log_likelihood - seq_filter_state.log_likelihood) print(f"Abs diff (log-likelihood): {ll_diff:.2e}") # Compare smoothed means smooth_mean_diff = jnp.max(jnp.abs(par_smooth_means - seq_smooth_means)) print(f"Max abs diff (smoothed means): {smooth_mean_diff:.2e}") # Compare smoothed covariances smooth_cov_diff = jnp.max(jnp.abs(par_smooth_covs - seq_smooth_covs)) print(f"Max abs diff (smoothed covs): {smooth_cov_diff:.2e}")

    Joseph-form covariance update¶

    The standard Kalman update computes the posterior covariance as $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{x,t \mid t} = (\mathbf{I} - \mathbf{G}_t \mathbf{H}) \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{x,t \mid t-1}$, but this can lose symmetry or positive definiteness due to round-off. The Joseph form is more robust:

    $$\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{x,t \mid t} = (\mathbf{I} - \mathbf{G}_t \mathbf{H}) \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{x,t \mid t-1} (\mathbf{I} - \mathbf{G}_t \mathbf{H})^\top + \mathbf{G}_t \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\varepsilon \mathbf{G}_t^\top$$

    We manually compute the Kalman gain $\mathbf{G}_t$ at one time step and compare both formulas.

    In [7]:
    Copied! 
    # Pick a time step to illustrate
step = 50
# Σ_x,t|t−1 ∈ ℝ^{D_x×D_x}
predicted_covariance = par_filter_state.predicted_covs[step]  # (2, 2)
# μ_x,t|t−1 ∈ ℝ^{D_x}
predicted_mean = par_filter_state.predicted_means[step]  # (2,)

# Compute Kalman gain G = Σ_x,t|t−1 Hᵀ (H Σ_x,t|t−1 Hᵀ + Σ_ε)⁻¹
# Σ_y,t = H Σ_x,t|t−1 Hᵀ + Σ_ε
obs_covariance = (
    obs_operator @ predicted_covariance @ obs_operator.T + obs_noise_covariance
)
# G_t = Σ_x,t|t−1 Hᵀ Σ_y,t⁻¹
gain = predicted_covariance @ obs_operator.T @ jnp.linalg.inv(obs_covariance)

print(f"Time step {step}:")
print(f"Kalman gain G =\n{gain}")

# Standard update: (I - GH) Σ_x,t|t−1
# Σ_x,t|t = (I − G_t H) Σ_x,t|t−1
state_size = predicted_covariance.shape[0]
standard_covariance = (jnp.eye(state_size) - gain @ obs_operator) @ predicted_covariance

# Joseph-form update
# Σ_x,t|t = (I − G_t H) Σ_x,t|t−1 (I − G_t H)ᵀ + G_t Σ_ε G_tᵀ
joseph_covariance = gaussx.joseph_update(
    predicted_covariance, gain, obs_operator, obs_noise_covariance
)

print(f"\nStandard update Σ_x,t|t =\n{standard_covariance}")
print(f"\nJoseph update Σ_x,t|t =\n{joseph_covariance}")
max_difference = jnp.max(jnp.abs(standard_covariance - joseph_covariance))
print(f"\nMax abs difference: {max_difference:.2e}")

# The Joseph form guarantees symmetry
standard_asymmetry = jnp.max(jnp.abs(standard_covariance - standard_covariance.T))
joseph_asymmetry = jnp.max(jnp.abs(joseph_covariance - joseph_covariance.T))
print(f"\nStandard symmetry error: {standard_asymmetry:.2e}")
print(f"Joseph symmetry error:   {joseph_asymmetry:.2e}")
    # Pick a time step to illustrate step = 50 # Σ_x,t|t−1 ∈ ℝ^{D_x×D_x} predicted_covariance = par_filter_state.predicted_covs[step] # (2, 2) # μ_x,t|t−1 ∈ ℝ^{D_x} predicted_mean = par_filter_state.predicted_means[step] # (2,) # Compute Kalman gain G = Σ_x,t|t−1 Hᵀ (H Σ_x,t|t−1 Hᵀ + Σ_ε)⁻¹ # Σ_y,t = H Σ_x,t|t−1 Hᵀ + Σ_ε obs_covariance = ( obs_operator @ predicted_covariance @ obs_operator.T + obs_noise_covariance ) # G_t = Σ_x,t|t−1 Hᵀ Σ_y,t⁻¹ gain = predicted_covariance @ obs_operator.T @ jnp.linalg.inv(obs_covariance) print(f"Time step {step}:") print(f"Kalman gain G =\n{gain}") # Standard update: (I - GH) Σ_x,t|t−1 # Σ_x,t|t = (I − G_t H) Σ_x,t|t−1 state_size = predicted_covariance.shape[0] standard_covariance = (jnp.eye(state_size) - gain @ obs_operator) @ predicted_covariance # Joseph-form update # Σ_x,t|t = (I − G_t H) Σ_x,t|t−1 (I − G_t H)ᵀ + G_t Σ_ε G_tᵀ joseph_covariance = gaussx.joseph_update( predicted_covariance, gain, obs_operator, obs_noise_covariance ) print(f"\nStandard update Σ_x,t|t =\n{standard_covariance}") print(f"\nJoseph update Σ_x,t|t =\n{joseph_covariance}") max_difference = jnp.max(jnp.abs(standard_covariance - joseph_covariance)) print(f"\nMax abs difference: {max_difference:.2e}") # The Joseph form guarantees symmetry standard_asymmetry = jnp.max(jnp.abs(standard_covariance - standard_covariance.T)) joseph_asymmetry = jnp.max(jnp.abs(joseph_covariance - joseph_covariance.T)) print(f"\nStandard symmetry error: {standard_asymmetry:.2e}") print(f"Joseph symmetry error: {joseph_asymmetry:.2e}")

    SSM natural parameters¶

    A linear-Gaussian state-space model defines a joint Gaussian $p(\mathbf{x}_0, \ldots, \mathbf{x}_{T-1})$ on the stacked state $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^{T D_x}$ whose precision matrix $\boldsymbol{\Lambda}_x$ is block-tridiagonal. The function ssm_to_naturals extracts the natural parameters $(\boldsymbol{\Lambda}_x \boldsymbol{\mu}_x, -\frac{1}{2} \boldsymbol{\Lambda}_x)$ where $-\frac{1}{2} \boldsymbol{\Lambda}_x$ is stored as a BlockTriDiag operator.

    The API takes the chain in the same layout as gaussx.MarkovGaussian: A and Q of shape (T-1, D_x, D_x), where Q[t] is the model-noise covariance $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{\eta,t+1}$ of the transition $\mathbf{x}_t \to \mathbf{x}_{t+1}$, and the initial covariance $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{x,0}$ separately.

    In [8]:
    Copied! 
    # F_t = F for t = 0, …, T − 2
transition_full = jnp.tile(transition, (num_steps - 1, 1, 1))
# Σ_η,t+1 = Σ_η for t = 0, …, T − 2
model_noise_full = jnp.tile(model_noise_covariance, (num_steps - 1, 1, 1))

print("F_full shape:", transition_full.shape)
print("Σ_η_full shape:", model_noise_full.shape)
    # F_t = F for t = 0, …, T − 2 transition_full = jnp.tile(transition, (num_steps - 1, 1, 1)) # Σ_η,t+1 = Σ_η for t = 0, …, T − 2 model_noise_full = jnp.tile(model_noise_covariance, (num_steps - 1, 1, 1)) print("F_full shape:", transition_full.shape) print("Σ_η_full shape:", model_noise_full.shape)

Σ_η_full shape: (199, 2, 2)

    # Convert to natural parameters
# (Λ_x μ_x, −½ Λ_x)
natural_linear, natural_precision = gaussx.ssm_to_naturals(
    transition_full, model_noise_full, prior_mean, prior_covariance
)

print("natural_linear shape:", natural_linear.shape)
print("natural_precision type:", type(natural_precision).__name__)
print("natural_precision diagonal shape:", natural_precision.diagonal.shape)
print("natural_precision sub_diagonal shape:", natural_precision.sub_diagonal.shape)
    # Convert to natural parameters # (Λ_x μ_x, −½ Λ_x) natural_linear, natural_precision = gaussx.ssm_to_naturals( transition_full, model_noise_full, prior_mean, prior_covariance ) print("natural_linear shape:", natural_linear.shape) print("natural_precision type:", type(natural_precision).__name__) print("natural_precision diagonal shape:", natural_precision.diagonal.shape) print("natural_precision sub_diagonal shape:", natural_precision.sub_diagonal.shape)

    Inspect the BlockTriDiag structure¶

    The BlockTriDiag operator stores (T, D_x, D_x) diagonal blocks and (T-1, D_x, D_x) sub-diagonal blocks. Its dense representation is a $(T D_x \times T D_x)$ matrix with the characteristic banded sparsity pattern of a Gauss-Markov chain.

    In [10]:
    Copied! 
    # Materialize the dense precision matrix (small enough for T=200, D_x=2)
dense_precision = natural_precision.as_matrix()
print("Dense precision shape:", dense_precision.shape)
    # Materialize the dense precision matrix (small enough for T=200, D_x=2) dense_precision = natural_precision.as_matrix() print("Dense precision shape:", dense_precision.shape)
    Dense precision shape: (400, 400)
    In [11]:
    Copied! 
    # Round-trip: convert back to SSM parameters
transition_rt, model_noise_rt, prior_mean_rt, prior_covariance_rt = (
    gaussx.naturals_to_ssm(natural_linear, natural_precision, initial_in_q=False)
)

print(
    "Round-trip F max error:", jnp.max(jnp.abs(transition_rt - transition_full)).item()
)
print(
    "Round-trip Σ_η max error:",
    jnp.max(jnp.abs(model_noise_rt - model_noise_full)).item(),
)
print(
    "Round-trip μ_x,0 max error:", jnp.max(jnp.abs(prior_mean_rt - prior_mean)).item()
)
print(
    "Round-trip Σ_x,0 max error:",
    jnp.max(jnp.abs(prior_covariance_rt - prior_covariance)).item(),
)
    # Round-trip: convert back to SSM parameters transition_rt, model_noise_rt, prior_mean_rt, prior_covariance_rt = ( gaussx.naturals_to_ssm(natural_linear, natural_precision, initial_in_q=False) ) print( "Round-trip F max error:", jnp.max(jnp.abs(transition_rt - transition_full)).item() ) print( "Round-trip Σ_η max error:", jnp.max(jnp.abs(model_noise_rt - model_noise_full)).item(), ) print( "Round-trip μ_x,0 max error:", jnp.max(jnp.abs(prior_mean_rt - prior_mean)).item() ) print( "Round-trip Σ_x,0 max error:", jnp.max(jnp.abs(prior_covariance_rt - prior_covariance)).item(), )

    SSM expectation parameters¶

    Given smoothed marginals $(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{x,t \mid T}, \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{x,t \mid T})$ and cross-covariances $[\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_x]_{t+1,t} = \mathrm{Cov}(\mathbf{x}_{t+1}, \mathbf{x}_t \mid \mathbf{y}_{1:T})$, we can compute the expectation parameters $(\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{x}], \mathbb{E}[\mathbf{x} \mathbf{x}^\top])$ of the joint Gaussian:

    • $\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{x}]$ (concatenated means)
    • $\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{x} \mathbf{x}^\top]$: a BlockTriDiag with diagonal blocks $\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{x}_t \mathbf{x}_t^\top]$ and sub-diagonal blocks $\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{x}_{t+1} \mathbf{x}_t^\top]$

    The cross-covariance is computed from the smoother gain: $[\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_x]_{t+1,t} = \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{x,t+1 \mid T} \mathbf{G}_{\text{smooth},t}^\top$ where $\mathbf{G}_{\text{smooth},t} = \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{x,t \mid t} \mathbf{F}^\top \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{x,t+1 \mid t}^{-1}$.

    In [12]:
    Copied! 
    # Compute cross-covariances from filter/smoother outputs
# G_smooth,t = Σ_x,t|t Fᵀ Σ_x,t+1|t⁻¹
# [Σ_x]_t+1,t = Σ_x,t+1|T G_smooth,tᵀ


def compute_cross_covs(filter_state, smoothed_covs, transition):
    """Compute cross-covariances [Σ_x]_{t+1,t} = Σ_x,t+1|T G_smooth,tᵀ."""
    filtered_covs = filter_state.filtered_covs[:-1]  # (T-1, D_x, D_x)
    predicted_covs = filter_state.predicted_covs[1:]  # (T-1, D_x, D_x)
    smoothed_covs_next = smoothed_covs[1:]  # (T-1, D_x, D_x)

    def _one_step(filtered_cov, predicted_cov, smoothed_cov_next):
        # G_smooth,t = Σ_x,t|t Fᵀ Σ_x,t+1|t⁻¹
        smoother_gain = jnp.linalg.solve(
            predicted_cov.T, (filtered_cov @ transition.T).T
        ).T
        # Σ_x,t+1|T G_smooth,tᵀ
        return smoothed_cov_next @ smoother_gain.T

    return jax.vmap(_one_step)(filtered_covs, predicted_covs, smoothed_covs_next)


cross_covs = compute_cross_covs(par_filter_state, par_smooth_covs, transition)
print("Cross-covariances shape:", cross_covs.shape)

    Visualizations¶

    BlockTriDiag sparsity pattern¶

    The precision matrix of a Gauss-Markov chain has a characteristic block-tridiagonal sparsity pattern. We visualize the first few blocks to see this structure clearly.

    In [15]:
    Copied! 
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 5))

# Sparsity pattern of the precision (show first 20 blocks = 40x40)
n_show = min(20, num_steps)
d_show = n_show * state_size
prec_sub = dense_precision[:d_show, :d_show]

ax = axes[0]
ax.spy(jnp.abs(prec_sub) > 1e-12, markersize=1, color="C0")
ax.set_title(f"BlockTriDiag sparsity (first {n_show} blocks)")
ax.set_xlabel("Column index")
ax.set_ylabel("Row index")

# Zoom into a 3-block region to see the structure
n_zoom = 3
d_zoom = n_zoom * state_size
prec_zoom = dense_precision[:d_zoom, :d_zoom]

ax = axes[1]
im = ax.imshow(prec_zoom, cmap="RdBu_r", aspect="equal")
ax.set_title(f"Precision blocks (first {n_zoom} blocks)")
ax.set_xlabel("Column index")
ax.set_ylabel("Row index")
# Draw block boundaries

    ax.axhline(i * state_size - 0.5, color="k", lw=0.5, ls="--")
    ax.axvline(i * state_size - 0.5, color="k", lw=0.5, ls="--")
plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax, shrink=0.8)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

    Summary¶

    • Parallel Kalman filter: gaussx.parallel_kalman_filter produces identical results to the sequential gaussx.kalman_filter but uses dense array operations suited for GPU/TPU acceleration.
    • Parallel RTS smoother: gaussx.parallel_rts_smoother likewise matches the sequential smoother.
    • Joseph-form update: gaussx.joseph_update computes the Kalman covariance update in a numerically stable form that preserves symmetry and positive-definiteness.
    • Natural parameters: gaussx.ssm_to_naturals extracts the block-tridiagonal precision (as a BlockTriDiag operator) and the linear natural parameter from SSM matrices. gaussx.naturals_to_ssm inverts this exactly.
    • Expectation parameters: gaussx.ssm_to_expectations converts smoother marginals (means, covariances, cross-covariances) to expectation parameters with BlockTriDiag second moments. gaussx.expectations_to_ssm inverts this exactly.
    • The BlockTriDiag operator exploits Gauss-Markov sparsity for $O(T D_x^3)$ operations instead of $O((T D_x)^3)$ dense cost.

    References¶

    • Sarkka, S. & Garcia-Fernandez, A. F. (2021). Temporal parallelization of Bayesian smoothers. IEEE Trans. Automatic Control, 66(1), 299--306.
    • Kalman, R. E. (1960). A new approach to linear filtering and prediction problems. J. Basic Engineering, 82(1), 35--45.
    • Rauch, H. E., Tung, F., & Striebel, C. T. (1965). Maximum likelihood estimates of linear dynamic systems. AIAA Journal, 3(8), 1445--1450.
    • Sarkka, S. (2013). Bayesian Filtering and Smoothing. Cambridge University Press.
